title.narrative: Presidente Nicolau Lobato International Airport Expansion Project

description.narrative:
The Presidente Nicolau Lobato International Airport (PNLIA) has a runway of 1,850 meters (m) in length with a pavement width of 30m. The runway can accommodate Code C aircrafts such as B737 and A320, but operations of these aircrafts are under significant restrictions on payload because the length of the runway is short. The existing runway also does not have the ICAO specified Runway End Safety Areas (RESA), which is at least 90m long and required for safe aerodrome operation. These two issues pose challenges in route development of the PNLIA for better air connectivity of the country because airlines have to take into consideration commercial penalty by operating with reduced passenger load factors (i.e., less seat occupied) and consider extra safety measures. The current Air Traffic Control Tower (ATCT) is also in poor condition and does not fully meet the requirements even for the existing runway.
The project will be aligned with the following impact: national productivity improved by ensuring better connectivity of its people within and outside of the country. The proposed outcome is improved efficiency and safety of goods and people's movements.

Based on the Government of Timor-Leste's official "120 days of Commitments by the Ninth Constitutional Government" document, released in 2023 (https://www.laohamutuk.org/misc/gov9/231214-120dias-relatorioEn.pdf), the project is under review and government will decide in what terms it should proceed of if public interest determines that it should not be executed. Aside from this document, the government has not released any other official document in relation to the project's implementation.
DB CONTRACT PACKAGE: The design build (DB) contract was signed on 29 May 2023 and cleared by Court of Audit on 6 July 2023. However, the Ministry of Transport and Communication (MOTC) decided to hold off further process with regard to the DB contract. In a letter dated 23 August 2024, MOTC provided ADB with copy of the signed contract between MOTC and PT. Waskita Karya (Persero) Tbk for the design build contract package. ADB created the contract record and informed the government through fax dated 26 August 2024. Government has issued a notice to proceed to the DB contractor on 13 January 2025 (ADB has yet to receive copy of the issued NTP). ADB is also awaiting government's submission of withdrawal application for the 15% advance payment to the DB contractor. Detailed design works is ongoing. The contractor has also started removal of existing structures, relocation of existing facilities, and clearing and grubbing activities.
CSC CONTRACT PACKAGE: Negotiation with the first ranked construction supervision consultant (CSC) has been completed and contract is for CAFI approval. ADB mission in August 2023 reminded the government that the CSC has to be onboard prior to mobilization of the DB contractor. As of end-June 2025, contract award is still pending as CAFI approval is still pending. The government through letter dated 2 June 2025 requested ADB's no objection for the appointment of a temporary supervision team leader/engineer to provide oversight and safeguards implementation during the initial mobilization phase and maintain compliance with project standards and provide coordination support to project stakeholders for an estimated period of three months or until early September 2025. ADB through a letter dated 5 June 2025 provided the requested no objection. It is expected that the DB-contractor's firm work program for both the design and build components will be available after the CSC is recruited and be on board by September 2025. CSC contract was signed on 24 July 2025. NTP was issued on 8 August 2025 and services commenced on 13 August 2025.
PMC: MOTC on 9 September 2024 issued the notice to commence to the project management consultant (PMC). Subsequently, PMC has already mobilized its team leader and deputy team leader in late September 2024.
A bi-weekly meeting among government, PMC, ADB, and other development partners, to update each other on the progress of the entire airport development project has been initiated with the first meeting held on 19 February 2025. ADB has recommended the conduct of smaller meetings to focus on matters related to the components under the ADB loans.
Data Source: Contractor's reports on employee hiring and retention related to the project, disaggregated by sex and job category
